Serilog._comment: Defaults wired by UseCardscapeSerilog(). RootPath is resolved against the API content root when relative. Database.Enabled is a no-op today; the ILogEventSink placeholder ships compiled and waits for the schema ADR before flipping the switch.

Internal._comment: Service-to-service shared secret for the MCP-to-API broadcast webhook (POST /api/internal/broadcast). The MCP server is configured with the same value via Cardscape:Internal:Secret. Required in production; if absent, the broadcast endpoint short-circuits with 503.

Cardscape._comment: Operator-tunable subsystems. Full rationale, defaults, and trade-offs are documented in docs/operations/06-configurable-subsystems.md. Every subsection below can be overridden by environment variables (use double-underscore instead of colon, e.g. Cardscape__Api__AdminAuthorization__CacheAdminClaim=false).

AdminAuthorization._comment: Controls how the /api/admin/* endpoints verify that the caller is a system administrator. See docs/operations/06-configurable-subsystems.md#admin-authorization for the full trade-off discussion.

Infrastructure._comment: Backend selection for the in-memory helpers that have an optional distributed implementation. InMemory is the default for every subsystem so a single-instance deploy needs no extra infrastructure. Switching a subsystem to Redis is operator-driven: the implementation class is wired in DI on application start, the connection string is read once, and the IConnectionMultiplexer is shared across every subsystem that opted in.

Redis._comment: Connection settings shared by every Redis-backed subsystem. REQUIRED when at least one Backend is 'Redis' (startup fails with a clear error otherwise); ignored otherwise.

RateLimiter._comment: The per-API-token rate limiter. The InMemory implementation keeps a bucket dictionary per process; the Redis implementation shares one bucket across every API instance via a Lua-scripted token bucket. Set Backend to 'Redis' on a multi-instance deploy where the soft per-instance guard is too soft. See docs/operations/06-configurable-subsystems.md#rate-limiter-backend.

PendingTotpStore._comment: The one-shot token that bridges the password step and the TOTP step of the 2FA login flow. The InMemory implementation is a per-process dictionary; the Redis implementation survives process restarts and lets any API instance complete a 2FA challenge that another instance started. Set Backend to 'Redis' on a multi-instance deploy OR when you want TOTP challenges to survive an in-place restart. See docs/operations/06-configurable-subsystems.md#pending-2fa-store-backend.
